original_question: Find the asymptotic value of Dlines(m,n), the minimum number of distinct distances between m points on one line and n points on another planar line when the two lines are neither parallel nor orthogonal.
target_in_paper: Section 5, Problem 16 of arXiv:1406.1949 v3: the bipartite distinct-distances problem for two lines in R^2 that are neither parallel nor orthogonal. In the June 7, 2014 version of the same survey, the closely related official formulation appears as Problem 14 for the balanced case Dlines(n), with the asymmetric m,n bound discussed immediately before it.
correct_elements: The draft already captures the core intent of the paper very well: it asks for the asymptotic minimum number of distinct distances in the two-line bipartite setting, and it includes the crucial exclusion that the two lines are neither parallel nor orthogonal.
missing_details: Dlines(m,n) should be defined explicitly, since this notation is not standard outside the paper's context.
The minimum must be stated as ranging over all admissible choices of two lines l1,l2 and finite point sets P1 subset l1, P2 subset l2 with |P1|=m and |P2|=n.
The ambient space should be specified as the real Euclidean plane R^2.
The distance should be specified as ordinary Euclidean distance.
It should be stated explicitly that only bipartite distances {||p-q|| : p in P1, q in P2} are counted, not distances within P1 or within P2.
The lines are not fixed in advance; the minimization is uniform over all pairs of lines whose angle is neither 0 nor pi/2.
m and n should be declared to be positive integers.
For a two-parameter problem, 'asymptotic value' should mean the order of growth up to absolute multiplicative constants as a function of m and n.
By symmetry one may assume m <= n without loss of generality, but this is a convention, not part of the definition.
refined_question: For positive integers m and n, let D_lines(m,n) be the minimum possible cardinality of the set {||p-q|| : p in P1, q in P2}, where P1 and P2 are finite subsets of R^2 with |P1|=m and |P2|=n, P1 is contained in a line l1, P2 is contained in a line l2, and l1 and l2 are neither parallel nor orthogonal. Here only Euclidean distances between a point of P1 and a point of P2 are counted. Determine the asymptotic order of growth of D_lines(m,n) as a function of m and n.
justification: The relevant target is the survey's open problem on bipartite distinct distances for point sets lying on two lines. The surrounding context first defines bipartite distinct distances by counting only distances across P1 x P2, then singles out parallel and orthogonal lines as exceptional cases where only Theta(n) distances may occur, and finally asks for the asymptotic value in the nonparallel, nonorthogonal regime. Your draft is therefore very close to the paper's actual intent. The main refinements needed are to make the minimization explicit, specify that the setting is over R^2 with Euclidean distance, and spell out that only cross-set distances are counted. I have kept the scope exactly at the two-line problem and have not broadened it to curves or higher dimensions.
